MQL5 -> PYTHON CONVERSION LOG
=============================

Source folders (on this machine):
  MQL5 Codebase/MQL5 Include                      156 files (154 .mqh + 2 .mq5)
  MQL5 Codebase/MQL5 Indicators                   6,447 .mq5 in 5,121 folders

Python destinations:
  backtester/indicators/mql5_include/   ports of the include libraries
  python_indicators/                    converted indicators (one plugin file each)
  tests/test_mql5_include.py            tests for the include ports (pytest)
  backtester/mql5/                      the MQL5 -> Python converter and MQL5 runtime
  python_indicators/mql5_codebase/      the batch-converted Codebase indicators
                                        (+ _index.json, conversion_results.csv)
  tests/test_mql5_translator.py         tests for the converter (pytest)

Contents
  A. Conventions used by every port
  B. Phase 1: MQL5 Include, file by file (all 156)
  C. Standard MT5 includes the indicators use that are NOT in the Include folder
  D. Phase 2: indicator conversions (running log; batch of all 6,447 from 2026-10-31)
  E. Verification of the converter and of the converted indicators


A. CONVENTIONS
--------------
* Faithful, line-by-line ports. MQL class, method and function names and
  argument orders are kept, so an indicator port reads like its .mq5.
* MQL5 semantics come from mql5_include/mql_runtime.py:
    - EMPTY_VALUE = DBL_MAX (1.797e308); converted to NaN only when a plugin
      returns its plot arrays (NaN = "draw nothing" in this app);
    - idiv/imod = C integer division (truncates toward zero);
    - fdiv = IEEE float division (x/0 = inf, 0/0 = nan instead of an exception);
    - 32-bit wrap-around (as_int32) where the source relies on int overflow.
* Series indexing (ArraySetAsSeries true): kept wherever the source uses
  it (index 0 = newest bar). Plugins return forward arrays (index 0 = oldest).
* Source bugs that change the numbers are REPRODUCED, not fixed, and are
  documented in the module docstring ("Faithfully reproduced ..."). The goal
  is identical output to MetaTrader.
* Terminal data functions (CopyRates, iClose(symbol, tf, shift), SymbolInfo*,
  MarketInfo, ...) read from mql5_include/terminal.py: a stand-in terminal
  that holds bar DataFrames per (symbol, timeframe) plus a contract spec.
* Chart-object, canvas and GUI code has no counterpart: this app draws an
  indicator from the arrays it returns, not from chart objects. Pure-drawing
  includes are therefore not ported, and object calls inside ported code are
  no-ops.

Status legend
  PORTED      full port; the module docstring lists any quirks
  PARTIAL     the computing part is ported; terminal/account/UI parts are not
  SAME AS     identical or near-identical copy of another file; one module
              covers both
  NOT PORTED  no computing content for a backtester indicator (reason given)
  INDICATOR   an .mq5 that sits in the Include folder; converted as a plugin

D. PHASE 2: INDICATOR CONVERSIONS
---------------------------------
Format per entry:
  <source .mq5 (path under MQL5 Codebase)>  -> python_indicators/<file>.py  [STATUS]
  (batch entries: -> python_indicators/mql5_codebase/<module>.py)
      notes: plots, includes used, quirks reproduced, test result
Status: CONVERTED | CONVERTED (approx: reason) | SKIPPED (reason) | FAILED (reason)

2026-10-20
MQL5 Include/x2ma_osc.mq5  -> python_indicators/x2ma_osc.py  [CONVERTED]
    class X2MAOsc "X2MA_Osc", separate pane, 1 line + level 0.
    Uses smooth_algorithms CXMA twice in series mode (set=True), a ring of
    n_period values, interpolation to -50..+50. Warm-up kept: the range window
    starts with zeros/EMPTY_VALUE, so the first n_period drawn bars sit near
    -50 (as in MT5). PriceShift input is never used by the source; omitted.
    Verified identical to an independent forward-indexed reference; causal
    (tests/test_mql5_include.py).

MQL5 Include/HLCrossSigForWPR.mq5  -> python_indicators/hl_cross_sig_for_wpr.py  [CONVERTED]
    class HLCrossSigForWPR "HL Cross Signal for WPR", price pane, 8 arrow plots
    (buy/sell signals, stops, takes, entry levels).
    Kept: empty slots are 0 (NULL) and the logic reads them that way (e.g.
    close >= SellStop[prev] is true while the sell stop is unset); zeros are
    turned into gaps only for drawing. Stops/takes ratchet only while the
    opposite side is unset. Spread term uses each bar's stored spread x point.
    iMA (SMA of median price), iWPR and iATR from backtester/indicators/mql5.py.
    Causal (tests/test_mql5_include.py).

2026-10-31  BATCH: every .mq5 in MQL5 Codebase/MQL5 Indicators
------------------------------------------------------------

Method. Every .mq5 was translated by the converter in backtester/mql5 (lexer, preprocessor,
parser, translator; see backtester/mql5/README.md). The Python follows the MQL5 source
statement by statement and runs on an emulation of the MQL5 standard library, so the
indicator logic is MetaTrader's own. Include files without global state (SmoothAlgorithms,
MovingAverages, ...) became shared modules in backtester/mql5/lib.

Testing. Each converted indicator was loaded with the app's plugin loader and run on 3,000
synthetic EURUSD H1 bars (weekends excluded). Checked: it computes without error, it draws
something, and the values on the first 2,000 bars equal those computed with all 3,000 bars
(otherwise it repaints / looks ahead, which MT5 indicators like ZigZag do by design).
Verified against independent references: the SmoothAlgorithms classes (all 10 methods)
match the hand port in backtester/indicators/mql5_include exactly; see section E.

E. VERIFICATION
---------------

E1. Converter unit tests: tests/test_mql5_translator.py (pytest). Small MQL5
    programs are converted and run: C integer division/modulo, series indexing,
    static locals, struct value copies, switch fall-through, nested ternaries,
    input overrides, the CopyTime datetime/position overloads, and an iMA handle
    checked against a rolling mean.

E2. Built-in indicator handles vs the app's own MT5 formulas
    (backtester/indicators/mql5.py), 2,500 synthetic H1 bars, after bar 300:
      iMA SMA            compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 2.66e-15
      iMA EMA            compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 0
      iRSI               compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 0
      iATR               compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 6.51e-18
      iCCI               compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 6.72e-11
      iMomentum          compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 0
      iStochastic main   compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 0
      iMACD main         compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 0
      iADX               compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 2.84e-14
      iSAR               compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 0.00354
      iWPR               compared  2200 bars, max |diff| = 0
    iSAR differs only on the last (still forming) bar, where the MetaQuotes source
    and the app's formula treat the open bar differently; all closed bars match.

E3. SmoothAlgorithms (CXMA, all 10 methods) translated automatically vs the hand
    port in backtester/indicators/mql5_include: identical on every bar.

E4. Hand conversions made earlier (python_indicators/*.py) vs the batch version
    of the same .mq5. Score = share of the hand plot's bars the best-matching
    batch plot reproduces (rtol 1e-6). The batch splits color lines into one plot
    per color (p0_c0, p0_c1, ...), so a 3-color line scores about 0.33 although
    the values agree; low scores are explained per file.

E5. Batch test of every converted indicator (method in section D). Result counts:
      runs and draws                                                 5941
      no indicator plots (panels/objects/events only)                240
      runs, draws nothing on the test data                           117
      stops with an error in the converted code / unsupported feature 72
      stops with an MQL5 run-time error                              46
      slower than 90 s                                               6

E6. Known limits of the batch conversions
    - Other symbols: the emulated terminal only has the chart's symbol, so
      multi-currency indicators (baskets, correlation, arbitrage, currency
      strength, USDX) draw nothing or refuse to start.
    - DLL imports (MetaCOT/CFTC, Swiss Ephemeris, DF.dll, ...), ticks/order book,
      trading history, files and web requests are not available.
    - Chart objects: arrows, horizontal/trend lines and rectangles are drawn as
      'obj_*' plots; labels, text, canvases and control panels are not drawn.
    - Higher-timeframe series are built from the chart's own bars, so an
      indicator that expects more higher-timeframe history than the chart has
      (e.g. Reversal) can stop with 'array out of range'.
    - Source bugs are reproduced, not fixed (e.g. BreakTrend reads an
      uninitialised variable; LineBreakOnChart needs history before its start date).
    - Not converted (27 sources, listed in section D with the parser message):
      unions, interface templates (Generic collections), macros that expand to
      partial statements, and a few other constructs the parser does not accept.
    - Run-time gaps in converted code (counted in E5): vector/matrix types,
      calling an operator by name, string methods (s.Lower()), Canvas/CMatrix
      classes from includes that were not supplied.
